lines.text: Today you will make the computer repeat things hundreds of times without getting tired.
for i in range(5): runs the indented code five times.
The variable i counts for you: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.
Loops save you from copying the same line again and again.
range(1, 11) gives the numbers 1 to 10, because it stops just before the last number. range(10, 0, -1) counts backwards from 10 to 1.
The third number is the step.
while count > 0: repeats as long as the condition is True.
Use it when you do not know how many times you need.
Something inside must change, or it never stops.
If the condition never becomes False, the loop runs forever.
That is called an infinite loop.
Always change the variable inside the loop, like count -= 1.
We write the cheer only once, but the loop runs it three times.
The indented line is the body of the loop. It repeats each time.
This time the loop variable n goes from one up to five.
Range stops just before six, and each time we multiply n by four.
The while loop checks if count is still more than zero.
Each time round we take one away, so the countdown finally ends with Blast off.
Here we forgot to change count, so it stays five forever.
The Python Lab stops it for us, and the fix is one line: count -= 1.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
